rows.detail: The depth charts show the marker 'D' next to four players (MIA WR Chris Bell, SEA LT Charles Cross, SEA LG Quenton Nelson, GB LB Zaire Franklin). rows.title: The starter/backup question cannot be answered from official sources: nfl.com has no depth chart and no snap counts.
rows.detail: https://www.nfl.com/teams/washington-commanders/depth-chart/ returns a 404 (checked 2026-11-12). Club roster pages give position, number, height, weight, experience and college only. The injury page gives practice and game status only. No row on this site asserts that a player is a 2nd/3rd/4th-string replacement.

rows.title: The 1.5-point home-field value used for the 2026 originated lines is a model assumption, not an official value.
rows.detail: Home-field advantage is not published by the NFL. Our walk-forward historical estimate exists, but a 2026-only estimate cannot be separated from it with 9 games per club. The number is disclosed on the own-lines page next to every line it produced.

rows.title: Our model is less accurate than the closing line: spread MAE 10.502 vs 9.871 points; total 10.830 vs 10.470.
rows.detail: This is a negative result and it is the headline. It also means gate G4 fails for every strategy, so no strategy can be Qualified in this release. Presenting any of the originated lines as an edge would contradict the repository's own numbers.

rows.title: The model's 90% interval covers 89.34% of holdout games (fine) but the mean residual is +0.651 points (fails the pre-registered 0.5 bar).
rows.detail: The interval width is right and the centre is skewed toward the away team by about two-thirds of a point. Gate G3 therefore fails on the bias test only.

rows.title: The peer 2026 game archive in nfl-lab/data/games_2026.csv was missing 16 of 136 games (all of Week 9 plus the Week 8 Monday game).
rows.detail: The file held 120 rows. Using it as-is would have understated every club's games played by one or two and corrupted any rate statistic. The 16 missing games were read from the official week pages and added in nfl-edge/data/games_2026.json (peer file left untouched); the combined archive now reconciles to the official standings with 0 mismatches.

rows.title: The peer archive nfl-quant/data/predictions.csv contains 272 rows tagged season 2026, but the 2026 season is only at Week 10 (136 games played).
rows.detail: Rows for unplayed games may be fixtures, placeholders or mislabelled seasons. This session used that file only for 1999-2025 completed games with a recorded result, so no 2026 row affected any result published here. The inconsistency itself is unverified and is left for its owning session.

rows.title: Two datasets are corroborated by aggregate identity rather than by re-reading every page.
rows.detail: 120 of the 136 game scores come from a peer archive whose rows carry the official game-page URL; they are accepted because the aggregate W-L-T and PF-PA over all 136 games reproduces the official standings exactly for all 32 clubs. That is strong but not identical to reading every game page. The 16 restored games were read directly.

rows.title: The official team-statistics pages are HTML tables with no stable machine-readable export; every value on this site was transcribed by hand into JSON.
rows.detail: Transcription was defended with six league-wide identities (offence equals defence across the league for pass yards, pass TDs, rush yards, rush TDs, points and points against: 63,556 / 411 / 30,580 / 257 / 6,246 / 6,246). A single transposed digit inside a team row would not be caught by that test.

rows.title: Gate thresholds (300 bets, 60% positive seasons, |bias| < 0.5, p < 0.05) are research design choices, not official NFL values.
rows.detail: They are labelled as design choices and frozen in a versioned file before the backtest ran. They should be reviewed by a statistician before any reward is paid against them.
